questions.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders
FROM orders
questions.note: This counts every order in the dataset (99,441), whatever its status. Canceled and unavailable orders are not excluded because the question asks about the dataset, not sales.

questions.question: How many sellers are on the platform?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sellers
FROM sellers
questions.note: This counts every seller in the sellers table (3,095), including any who have no recorded sales.

questions.question: What is the average review score across all reviews?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
       COUNT(*) AS reviews
FROM order_reviews
questions.note: This averages every row in order_reviews, so each (review, order) pair counts once and no order-status filter is applied.

questions.question: What is the total value of all payments in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(payment_value), 2) AS total_payments
FROM order_payments
questions.note: This sums every payment row, about 16.01M BRL, including canceled and unavailable orders, because the question asks for all payments in the dataset.

questions.question: What is the average price of an order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_item_price
FROM order_items
questions.note: This averages the unit price (excluding freight) over all order items, without filtering by order status.

questions.question: How many products are there in each product category (English names)?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    COUNT(*) AS products
FROM products
GROUP BY COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
ORDER BY products DESC, category
questions.note: This counts every product in the catalog by its English category name, whether or not it ever sold, and reports products with no category as "unknown".

questions.question: How many distinct orders used each payment type?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY payment_type
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status, and an order paid with several methods is counted under each one, so the per-type counts add up to more than the total number of orders.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders have the status delivered?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') AS delivered_orders,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') / COUNT(*), 2) AS delivered_pct
FROM orders
questions.note: The denominator counts all orders of every status, including canceled and unavailable.

questions.question: What is the average number of installments for credit card payments?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(payment_installments), 2) AS avg_installments,
  COUNT(*) AS credit_card_payments
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card'
questions.note: This averages over every credit card payment row, regardless of order status, and does not filter out the 2 rows that have 0 installments.

questions.question: What is the average order value, measured as total payment per order, for orders that were not canceled or unavailable?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT p.order_id, SUM(p.payment_value) AS total_paid
    FROM order_payments p
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY p.order_id
)
SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(total_paid), 2) AS total_payments,
    ROUND(SUM(total_paid) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM order_pay
questions.note: Payments are summed per order first, so orders with several payment methods count once; the one order with no payment record is left out.

questions.question: What is the median total payment per order, across all orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT ROUND((PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_payment))::numeric, 2) AS median_payment,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM order_totals
questions.note: I read "across all orders" literally, so this includes every order with a payment row, including canceled and unavailable ones; the single order with no payment is left out.

questions.question: How many unique customers live in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers_rj
FROM customers
WHERE customer_state = 'RJ'
questions.note: This counts distinct people (`customer_unique_id`) whose address is in RJ on any of their orders, with no filter on order status.

questions.question: How many products weigh more than 10 kg?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_over_10kg
FROM products
WHERE product_weight_g > 10000
questions.note: This counts catalog products whose weight is strictly above 10,000 g, and products with no recorded weight are left out.

questions.question: How many order items cost more than 1,000 BRL?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS items_over_1000
FROM order_items
WHERE price > 1000
questions.note: This counts every unit priced above 1,000 BRL, excluding freight, across all order statuses, since the question does not limit it to sales.

questions.question: How many delivered orders arrived after their estimated delivery date?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date
questions.note: A delivered order counts as late when its customer delivery date is after its estimated delivery date; orders with no recorded delivery date are left out.

questions.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sp_sellers
FROM sellers
WHERE seller_state = 'SP'
questions.note: This counts every registered seller whose seller_state is 'SP', whether or not they made any sales.

questions.question: How many 1-star reviews include a comment message?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'reviews'
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT review_id) AS one_star_reviews_with_comment
FROM order_reviews
WHERE review_score = 1
  AND review_comment_message IS NOT NULL
  AND btrim(review_comment_message) <> ''
questions.note: This counts distinct `review_id` values because one review can cover several orders, and it treats blank or whitespace-only messages as having no comment.

questions.question: How many distinct orders were paid at least partly with a voucher?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS voucher_orders
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'voucher'
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, including canceled and unavailable, because the question is about payment method rather than sales.

questions.question: How many products have no category?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_without_category
FROM products
WHERE product_category_name_english IS NULL
questions.note: A product counts as having no category when its English category name is NULL. The data notes say this should be about 610 products.

questions.question: How many orders contain items from more than one seller?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS multi_seller_orders
FROM (
    SELECT order_id
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) > 1
) t
questions.note: This counts every order with items, whatever its status, so it should match the documented 1,278.

questions.question: List the cities in the state of Acre (AC) with the number of unique customers in each.
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city AS city,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
WHERE c.customer_state = 'AC'
GROUP BY c.customer_city
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC, city
questions.note: This counts distinct people (`customer_unique_id`) per customer city in AC across all orders, with no filter on order status.

questions.question: How many orders were approved more than 24 hours after they were placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_approved_after_24h
FROM orders
WHERE order_approved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND order_approved_at - order_purchase_timestamp > INTERVAL '24 hours'
questions.note: This counts orders of every status that have an approval timestamp; the 160 orders with no approval time are left out.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    oi.seller_id,
    s.seller_state,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders,
    COUNT(*) AS units_sold
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Seller revenue is the sum of item prices without freight, counting all orders except canceled and unavailable ones, because payments can't be split across sellers.

questions.question: What is the total revenue by customer state?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue here is the total customers paid (SUM of payment_value, which includes freight and installment interest), and canceled and unavailable orders are left out.

questions.question: Which customer state has the highest average freight value per order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.freight_value), 2) AS avg_freight_per_item,
    COUNT(*) AS items
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY avg_freight_per_item DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted only sales orders (canceled and unavailable orders excluded) and treated each order_items row as one item.

questions.question: How many orders came from each customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: This counts all orders of every status, including canceled and unavailable, because the question asks about orders rather than sales.

questions.question: Which 10 cities have the most unique customers?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city                     AS city,
    c.customer_state                    AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
GROUP BY c.customer_city, c.customer_state
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I grouped by city and state because some city names exist in more than one state. All orders count regardless of status, since the question asks about customers rather than sales.

questions.question: What is the average review score of orders paid with each payment type?
questions.sql:
WITH order_types AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, payment_type
    FROM order_payments
),
order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    ot.payment_type,
    COUNT(*)                  AS reviewed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(os.score), 2)   AS avg_review_score
FROM order_types ot
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = ot.order_id
GROUP BY ot.payment_type
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC
questions.note: Each order is averaged across its reviews first and counted once per payment type it used, so an order paid with a voucher plus a card counts under both types. All order statuses are included.

questions.question: What was the total freight charged on items in the furniture_decor category?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'total_freight'
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(oi.freight_value), 2) AS total_freight,
  COUNT(*) AS units
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE p.product_category_name_english = 'furniture_decor'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: This leaves out canceled and unavailable orders, following the sales rule; remove the status filter if you want freight on every item ever listed.

questions.question: What was the total revenue from customers in Minas Gerais (MG)?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2) AS mg_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE c.customer_state = 'MG'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: Revenue here is the total customers paid (payments, including freight and installment interest) on orders from MG, leaving out canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: What is the English name of the product category 'cama_mesa_banho'?
questions.sql:
SELECT product_category_name AS category_pt,
       product_category_name_english AS category_en
FROM category_translation
WHERE product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho'
questions.note: This reads the translation directly from the category_translation lookup table; the expected answer is bed_bath_table.

questions.question: Which product category has the highest average review score among categories with at least 100 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS order_score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
order_categories AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
)
SELECT oc.category,
       COUNT(*)                         AS reviewed_orders,
       ROUND(AVG(os.order_score), 2)    AS avg_review_score
FROM order_categories oc
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = oc.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY AVG(os.order_score) DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Each order counts once per category, using the average of its review scores when it has several reviews. Orders of every status are included.

questions.question: Which 3 sellers have the highest average review score among sellers with at least 50 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_scores AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
seller_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, seller_id
    FROM order_items
)
SELECT
    so.seller_id,
    s.seller_state                AS state,
    COUNT(*)                      AS reviewed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(os.score), 2)       AS avg_review_score
FROM seller_orders so
JOIN order_scores os ON os.order_id = so.order_id
JOIN sellers s       ON s.seller_id = so.seller_id
GROUP BY so.seller_id, s.seller_state
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50
ORDER BY AVG(os.score) DESC, COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 3
questions.note: Each order counts once per seller, and orders with several reviews use their mean score; ties are broken by the number of reviewed orders.

questions.question: How many unique customers bought from a seller located in a different state from their own?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS cross_state_customers
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c   ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN sellers s     ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND s.seller_state <> c.customer_state
questions.note: This counts a person if at least one item in any of their non-canceled, available orders came from a seller in a different state.

questions.question: What is the average price of items sold by sellers in each seller state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    s.seller_state                AS seller_state,
    COUNT(*)                      AS units_sold,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2)       AS avg_item_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders  o ON o.order_id  = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY s.seller_state
ORDER BY avg_item_price DESC
questions.note: This averages the price of each unit sold, excluding freight. It leaves out canceled and unavailable orders, following the sales rule.

questions.question: How many orders were placed in each year?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS year,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: This counts every order regardless of status, since the question asks about orders placed rather than sales. 2016 (Sep–Dec only, and sparse) and 2018 (data effectively ends in August) are incomplete years, so they are not directly comparable to 2017.

questions.question: Which month had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts all orders, whatever their status, by purchase month (year-month). To count only sales, add `WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')`.

questions.question: What was the average review score for each month of 2018, based on when the review was created?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', review_creation_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*)                                                       AS reviews,
    ROUND(AVG(review_score)::numeric, 2)                           AS avg_score
FROM order_reviews
WHERE review_creation_date >= '2018-01-01'
  AND review_creation_date <  '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: This averages every row in order_reviews (one row per review and order pair), with no filter on order status. The data feed effectively ends in August 2018, so any September or October rows will have few reviews and are unreliable.

questions.question: What was the total revenue in Q4 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS revenue_q4_2017
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-10-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
questions.note: Revenue here is the total customers paid (payments, including freight and installment interest) for orders placed from October to December 2017, excluding canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: On which day of the week (e.g. Monday) are the most orders placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    TO_CHAR(o.order_purchase_timestamp, 'FMDay') AS day_of_week,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
GROUP BY TO_CHAR(o.order_purchase_timestamp, 'FMDay')
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts every order placed, including canceled and unavailable ones, because the question asks about orders placed rather than sales.

questions.question: For each purchase month of 2017, what was the average delivery time in days (as a decimal) for delivered orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS purchase_month,
    COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: Delivery time is the exact time from purchase to delivery, converted to fractional days, and months are grouped by purchase date.

questions.question: How many orders were placed on Black Friday 2017 (November 24, 2017)?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS orders_placed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS valid_sales_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-24'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2017-11-25'
questions.note: `orders_placed` counts every order placed that day in Brazilian local time, and `valid_sales_orders` also shows the count without canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which product category had the largest increase in units sold from January–August 2017 to January–August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH units AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2017-09-01'
        ) AS units_2017,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
        ) AS units_2018
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    units_2017,
    units_2018,
    units_2018 - units_2017 AS unit_increase,
    ROUND(100.0 * (units_2018 - units_2017) / NULLIF(units_2017, 0), 2) AS pct_increase
FROM units
ORDER BY unit_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Units sold are counted as order_items rows from sales orders, which excludes canceled and unavailable orders. Products with no category are grouped as "unknown".

questions.question: Which month of 2018 had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2019-01-01'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted orders by purchase month and left out canceled and unavailable orders, following the sales rule; 2018-09 and 2018-10 are nearly empty because the data feed ends in August.

questions.question: Which 5 product categories had the largest drop in revenue from July 2018 to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_month AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(oi.price) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-08-01') AS jul_rev,
        SUM(oi.price) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01') AS aug_rev
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    ROUND(COALESCE(jul_rev, 0), 2)                          AS jul_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(COALESCE(aug_rev, 0), 2)                          AS aug_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(COALESCE(jul_rev, 0) - COALESCE(aug_rev, 0), 2)   AS revenue_drop,
    ROUND(100.0 * (COALESCE(aug_rev, 0) - COALESCE(jul_rev, 0))
          / NULLIF(jul_rev, 0), 2)                          AS pct_change
FROM cat_month
ORDER BY revenue_drop DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales (SUM of price, excluding freight) for orders that were not canceled or unavailable, and products with no category are grouped as "unknown".

questions.question: What was the month-over-month percentage change in the number of orders for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-12-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
with_prev AS (
    SELECT
        month,
        orders,
        LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT
    to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    orders,
    prev_orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / NULLIF(prev_orders, 0), 2) AS mom_pct_change
FROM with_prev
WHERE month >= DATE '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status and uses December 2017 as the baseline, so January 2018 also gets a month-over-month change.

questions.question: For each customer state, which product category generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_rev AS (
    SELECT c.customer_state AS state,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_state, COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT state, category, revenue,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
    FROM cat_rev
)
SELECT state,
       category AS top_category,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY state
questions.note:
Revenue here is item sales (SUM of price), since the question breaks revenue down by category.

Canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and products with no category are reported as "unknown". If two categories tie for first place in a state, both are shown.

questions.question: What was the 3-month moving average of monthly revenue for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
ma AS (
    SELECT month,
           revenue,
           AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg_3m
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(moving_avg_3m, 2) AS moving_avg_3m
FROM ma
WHERE month >= DATE '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: Revenue is total payments (`payment_value`) for orders that are not canceled or unavailable, and each month's moving average covers that month plus the two before it, so January 2018 includes November and December 2017.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers had the highest item revenue in 2018, and what percentage of total 2018 item revenue did each account for?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT oi.seller_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
)
SELECT sr.seller_id,
       s.seller_state,
       ROUND(sr.revenue, 2) AS item_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * sr.revenue / SUM(sr.revenue) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_2018_revenue
FROM seller_rev sr
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = sr.seller_id
ORDER BY sr.revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Item revenue is SUM(price) without freight. It counts all 2018 orders except canceled and unavailable ones, and the percentage is out of all sellers' 2018 item revenue. Note that 2018 data effectively ends in August.

questions.question: For 2017 and 2018 separately, what were the top 3 product categories by units sold?
questions.sql:
WITH units AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS yr,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) AS units_sold
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT yr, category, units_sold,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY yr ORDER BY units_sold DESC) AS rnk
    FROM units
)
SELECT yr AS year, rnk AS rank, category, units_sold
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 3
ORDER BY year, rank
questions.note: Canceled and unavailable orders are excluded. Ties may return more than 3 rows per year. The 2018 figures cover only January to August, plus a handful of September and October orders, because the data feed ends there.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders came from each customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(*) AS orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY pct_of_orders DESC
questions.note: Because the question says "all orders," this counts every order regardless of status, including canceled and unavailable ones.

questions.question: Which month in 2017 had the largest increase in orders compared with the previous month?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
changes AS (
    SELECT month,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders,
       orders - prev_orders AS increase,
       ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / prev_orders, 2) AS pct_increase
FROM changes
WHERE prev_orders IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts all orders placed, regardless of status, and only compares months within 2017. January is excluded because December 2016 had just 1 order, which would create an artificial spike.

questions.question: For each seller state, which seller has the highest revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT s.seller_state,
           oi.seller_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY s.seller_state, oi.seller_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT seller_state,
           seller_id,
           revenue,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
    FROM seller_rev
)
SELECT seller_state AS state,
       seller_id AS top_seller,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Seller revenue is SUM(order_items.price) without freight, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded. If two sellers tie for first in a state, both are shown.

questions.question: What was our revenue in 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS revenue_2017
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
questions.note: Revenue here is total customer payments, including freight and installment interest, for orders placed in 2017, leaving out canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: What is the average delivery time?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_delivered_customer_date - order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
questions.note: Delivery time is measured in days from purchase to customer delivery, using only delivered orders that have a delivery date.

questions.question: What was revenue by state in 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state                         AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)               AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid), 2)                   AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: This counts revenue as customer payments, grouped by the customer's state and by purchase date, with canceled and unavailable orders excluded. Note that 2018 data effectively ends in August, so the year is incomplete.

questions.question: How are we doing?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
rev AS (
    SELECT order_id, AVG(review_score) AS score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
base AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        o.order_id,
        c.customer_unique_id,
        p.paid,
        r.score,
        CASE WHEN o.order_status = 'delivered'
                  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
             THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0
        END AS delivery_days,
        CASE WHEN o.order_status = 'delivered'
                  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
             THEN (o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date)::int
        END AS is_late
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    LEFT JOIN rev r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT
        month,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)            AS orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id)  AS customers,
        SUM(paid)                           AS revenue,
        AVG(score)                          AS avg_review,
        AVG(delivery_days)                  AS avg_delivery_days,
        AVG(is_late) * 100                  AS late_pct
    FROM base
    GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
    to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM')                                   AS month,
    orders,
    customers,
    ROUND(revenue, 2)                                           AS revenue,
    ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month))
          / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2)   AS revenue_mom_pct,
    ROUND(revenue / NULLIF(orders, 0), 2)                       AS avg_order_value,
    ROUND(avg_review, 2)                                        AS avg_review,
    ROUND(avg_delivery_days, 2)                                 AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(late_pct, 2)                                          AS late_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month
questions.note: I read "how are we doing" as a monthly KPI scorecard covering sales orders, unique customers, payment revenue with month-over-month growth, AOV, review score and delivery performance, limited to the reliable 2017-01 to 2018-08 window.

questions.question: Who are our best customers?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_unique_id                              AS customer,
    MIN(c.customer_state)                             AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)                        AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid), 2)                            AS total_spent,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value,
    MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date             AS first_order,
    MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date             AS last_order
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I took "best customers" to mean the top 10 people (by `customer_unique_id`) ranked by total amount paid on non-canceled, available orders, and included order count and average order value for context.

questions.question: What was the recent trend?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders,
        SUM(op.paid) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    LEFT JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-09-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    orders,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
    ROUND(revenue / orders, 2) AS avg_order_value,
    ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month))
          / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS revenue_mom_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * (orders - LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month))
          / NULLIF(LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS orders_mom_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month
questions.note: I read "recent trend" as monthly sales (payment revenue and order count, excluding canceled and unavailable orders) over the last 12 reliable months, Sep 2017 to Aug 2018, and left out the near-empty Sep and Oct 2018 data.

questions.question: What is the age distribution of our customers?
questions.sql:
WITH first_purchase AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_ts
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
ref AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS ref_ts FROM orders
),
bucketed AS (
    SELECT CASE
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '90 days'  THEN '0-3 months'
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '180 days' THEN '3-6 months'
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '365 days' THEN '6-12 months'
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '730 days' THEN '12-24 months'
             ELSE '24+ months'
           END AS tenure_bucket,
           CASE
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '90 days'  THEN 1
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '180 days' THEN 2
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '365 days' THEN 3
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '730 days' THEN 4
             ELSE 5
           END AS sort_key
    FROM first_purchase f
    CROSS JOIN ref r
)
SELECT tenure_bucket,
       COUNT(*) AS customers,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_customers
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY tenure_bucket, sort_key
ORDER BY sort_key
questions.note:
The database has no age or birth-date data for customers, so an age distribution can't be computed. As a substitute, the query below shows customer **tenure**: how long ago each person first bought, measured from the last purchase in the dataset.

People are counted by `customer_unique_id`, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded. The data feed effectively ends in 2018-08, so the most recent bucket is slightly understated.

questions.question: How many people visited the Olist website in August 2018?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS buyers,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)           AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-08-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
questions.note:
The database has no website traffic or session data, so visits can't be counted. The closest available measure is the number of distinct people who placed an order in August 2018:

This counts purchasers, not visitors: it includes orders of any status and uses `customer_unique_id` to count people. The real number of site visitors would be much higher.

questions.question: Which marketing campaign brought in the most revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)                                         AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2)                                              AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY month
questions.note: The database has no marketing campaign, ad channel, or attribution data, so I can't say which campaign brought in the most revenue. As a stand-in, this query shows monthly revenue (payments, excluding canceled and unavailable orders, for the reliable months 2017-01 to 2018-08) so you can spot spikes that may line up with campaigns you know about, such as Black Friday in November 2017.

  table_name AS tbl,

WHERE table_schema = 'olist'
  AND grantee = current_user
